pack.title: Work chat tone traps
pack.description: Per my last message. Written words with an audience of the whole company.

scenarios.setting: Team channel. A peer corrects you in front of forty people.
scenarios.jab: Per my last message — that's not what we agreed.

replies.line: Linking the thread — let's align on the facts here.
replies.why: It moves the dispute from memory to receipts, in public, calmly.
replies.delivery: Keep the message factual and avoid quoting selectively to embarrass a colleague.

replies.why: Four words that replace the argument with the evidence.
replies.delivery: Keep the message factual and avoid quoting selectively to embarrass a colleague.

replies.line: Might be misaligned — dropping the thread so we can sync.
replies.why: Might plus the receipts keeps it collaborative while the facts do the work.
replies.delivery: Keep the message factual and avoid quoting selectively to embarrass a colleague.

replies.line: Let's invite the original thread into this conversation.
replies.why: Humor points to the shared record rather than mocking a colleague.
replies.delivery: Keep the message factual and avoid quoting selectively to embarrass a colleague.

trap.line: Don't correct me in the channel. DM me next time.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Clarify an agreement from the written record.

followUp.jab: That's still not what I meant.
followUp.line: Let's clarify the wording together and document the next step.
followUp.why: It moves from winning the interpretation to agreeing on what happens next.
followUp.delivery: Keep the message factual and avoid quoting selectively to embarrass a colleague.

scenarios.setting: DM from your manager, no context, 9:04am.

replies.line: What's the topic? I can check my availability.
replies.why: It requests context before committing to a task switch.
replies.delivery: Use a normal conversational tone; ask for context without making the message ominous.

replies.why: Available plus direct — the fastest route through the ambiguity.
replies.delivery: Use a normal conversational tone; ask for context without making the message ominous.

replies.line: Happy to understand what's needed; what's the topic and how urgent is it?
replies.why: It expresses willingness without promising immediate or constant availability.
replies.delivery: Use a normal conversational tone; ask for context without making the message ominous.

replies.line: My calendar would appreciate a hint; what's the topic?
replies.why: The joke asks for context without implying bad news.
replies.delivery: Use a normal conversational tone; ask for context without making the message ominous.

scenarios.goal: Ask for context before switching tasks.

followUp.line: What's the topic and urgency? I can tell you when I'm available.
followUp.why: It requests enough context to prioritize without implying constant availability.
followUp.delivery: Use a normal conversational tone; ask for context without making the message ominous.

scenarios.setting: A teammate messages after hours expecting you to start work immediately.
scenarios.jab: Can you jump on this tonight? It should be quick.
scenarios.goal: State when you are available for nonurgent work.

replies.line: I'm offline tonight. I'll review this tomorrow morning.
replies.why: It gives a clear availability boundary and next review time.
replies.delivery: State your availability once; use the real escalation process rather than inventing one.

replies.why: It states the schedule without inviting a negotiation about task length.
replies.delivery: State your availability once; use the real escalation process rather than inventing one.

replies.line: I can look tomorrow morning; please send the details so they're ready when I start.
replies.why: It offers a practical handoff without agreeing to work tonight.
replies.delivery: State your availability once; use the real escalation process rather than inventing one.

replies.line: My laptop has clocked out; tomorrow morning works.
replies.why: Humor concerns your working hours rather than the teammate's request.
replies.delivery: State your availability once; use the real escalation process rather than inventing one.

followUp.jab: But I really need it tonight.
followUp.line: I can't do tonight; if it's urgent, please use our agreed escalation route.
followUp.why: It maintains the boundary while directing genuinely urgent work to the team's process.
followUp.delivery: State your availability once; use the real escalation process rather than inventing one.
